articles.title: Brain stimulation helps socially anxious individuals control avoidance behaviors
articles.summary: A new study shows that targeted electrical brain stimulation can help socially anxious individuals overcome automatic avoidance behaviors. By synchronizing specific brain rhythms, the noninvasive technique improved participants' ability to control their emotional responses.

articles.title: Mystical experiences don’t explain the success of MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD
articles.summary: A new study suggests that positive emotional states, rather than profound mystical experiences, are the primary driver of symptom relief in MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD. The findings highlight how MDMA heals trauma differently than classic psychedelics.

articles.title: Why some young people stick with social causes while others fade away
articles.summary: Young adults drawn to social causes by deep moral convictions are more likely to stay engaged than those seeking social approval. New research reveals how political ideology and specific emotions shape whether a person’s activism lasts.

articles.title: Nut consumption is associated with sharper thinking skills and post-stroke brain health markers
articles.summary: People who eat more nuts tend to score higher on cognitive tests, particularly those with poor diets or exercise habits. New research suggests simply swapping unhealthy snacks for nuts could help protect brain health as we age.

articles.title: HEPA air purifiers may boost brain function after just one month
articles.summary: Adults aged 40 and older performed about 12% faster on a test of executive function after using a HEPA air purifier at home for one month. The findings suggest that cleaner indoor air could offer a simple way to help protect the brain from the effects of traffic-related pollution.

articles.summary: Why can some people easily ignore distractions while others struggle to stay on task? New research shows that the ability to maintain focus is a stable trait reflected in the rhythmic synchronization of large-scale brain networks.

articles.title: Researchers followed 400,000 kids for 20 years and found a lasting pre-K advantage
articles.summary: A 20-year study of 400,000 students found that children who attended public school pre-K earned better grades and test scores through high school than those in other childcare settings. Better-trained teachers and earlier exposure to structured classrooms may help explain why the advantage lasted so long.

articles.title: Adolescents report low regret and high satisfaction following gender-affirming chest surgery
articles.summary: Adolescents who undergo gender-affirming chest surgery experience high satisfaction and low regret, reporting outcomes similar to those of young adults. A new survey challenges political concerns that youth are likely to regret these procedures later in life.

articles.title: Smart nanoparticles light up brain cancer and destroy what surgery misses
articles.summary: Scientists created smart nanoparticles that can both illuminate hidden glioblastoma cells during surgery and destroy microscopic cancer left behind afterward. In mice, the treatment prevented recurrence and led to 100% survival at 60 days, though it has not yet been tested in humans.

articles.title: Scientists discover a brain “brake” that can shut down chronic pain
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a brain-based “brake” that can shut down chronic nerve pain in mice by calming an overactive pain circuit. Targeting this system more precisely could one day lead to powerful pain relief without affecting opioid receptors throughout the entire body.

articles.title: The tendency of conspiracy theorists to police others online is associated with narcissistic traits
articles.summary: New research suggests that people who endorse conspiracy theories frequently adopt the role of online "social vigilantes." This confrontational behavior—including arguing and online shaming—is closely linked to feelings of superiority and narcissistic desires for status.

articles.title: Study finds media coverage of the 2024 presidential race favored political spectacle over substantive policy debates
articles.summary: During the chaotic 2024 presidential election, major U.S. newspapers focused heavily on political strategy and legal battles rather than substantive policy. A recent study indicates that media coverage remained largely negative, except for a brief bump for Kamala Harris.

articles.summary: Two low doses of psilocybin helped chronically stressed rats recover their ability to experience pleasure while reducing anxiety. The psychedelic compound also promoted the birth of new neurons and normalized stress hormone levels.

articles.title: Brain scans reveal how artificial sweeteners affect our reward circuits differently than sugar
articles.summary: A new study reveals that while zero-calorie sweeteners generally affect the body like water, they trigger distinct activity in the brain’s reward centers compared to real sugar. Interestingly, some even delay stomach emptying without spiking blood sugar.
